item.title: 6 metal objects unearthed by shovel lead to discovery of 96 landmines
item.description:
Workers were digging soil to build a house. At that time they discovered six metal objects, found in the ground after hitting one of those with a shovel. Two days later, an army bomb-disposal team excavated the site and recovered 96 landmines.

The incident took place in Betbaria village of Gangni upazila in Meherpur.

The bomb-disposal team from Jashore Cantonment arrived at the site at around 1:30 pm today, Monday. Army personnel first examined the entire area with metal detectors before beginning excavation. Over nearly two hours, they recovered 96 mines, one after another.

Police and a team from the Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) cordoned off the area during the operation.

Gangni police station’s Inspector (Investigation) Shimul Kumar Das told Prothom Alo from the scene that the army bomb-disposal team arrived in Betbaria at noon and began excavating the site. Seventeen anti-tank mines and 79 anti-personnel mines were recovered. Most parts of the area were excavated.

After being recovered, the mines were taken to the nearby Madhugari field for disposal. The army was working to neutralise them there at the time of filing of this report.

Several police officials said an anti-personnel mine detonates when an object weighing 64 kgs is placed on it, while an anti-tank mine detonates under pressure from a heavier object.

The discovery of such a large stockpile of mines during excavation has caused considerable alarm in the area.

According to the army and police, the mines may have been buried by the Pakistan Army during the 1971 Liberation War for strategic purposes amid the wartime situation.

Mashiur Rahman, a local elder and former headteacher of a secondary school, said a Pakistani military camp had been located at Bengari field, about 10 kilometres from Betbaria village. Pakistani forces and freedom fighters fought a pitched battle there in 1971. The Pakistani forces were eventually forced to leave the area following a fierce attack by the freedom fighters.

The mines may have been left behind when the Pakistani forces withdrew, he said.

Several local elders and freedom fighters said Bengari field in Dharmadah village of Daulatpur upazila in Kushtia district lies about 2.5 kilometres from the site where the mines were discovered.

On 11–12 November 1971, freedom fighters fought a pitched battle with Pakistani forces at the field. Several freedom fighters and members of the allied forces, including Bir Protik recipient Waliul Hossain, were martyred in the bloody battle.

At one point, the Pakistani forces, overwhelmed by sustained attacks from the freedom fighters, fled towards Kushtia town through Betbaria village.

The mines may have been buried in an abandoned area of the village as they withdrew, the local elders and freedom fighters said.

Freedom fighter Golam Mostofa of Kajipur village in Kajipur union of Gangni upazila, who took part in the Bengari battle, told Prothom Alo by phone, “When we attacked the Pakistani force’s camp at Bengari in Daulatpur, the sun had not yet risen. Caught off guard by the sudden attack, the Pakistani forces fled towards Kushtia with their vehicles and tanks. We later captured the camp.

“The road where the mines were found in Betbaria was the route used by the Pakistani forces to flee with their weapons and equipment. They were attacked again in the Khalishakundi area on their way to Kushtia. Later, we blew up a bridge with explosives.”

Earlier, last Saturday, workers were digging soil on seven decimals of land owned by expatriate Bangladeshi Nuruzzaman Kalu in Betbaria village to construct a house. They noticed six metal objects while digging.

The objects were inscribed with the words: “PDFGL 63, Lot 37, Mine 1967.”

After being informed, police arrived at the site, cordoned off the area and strengthened security. Police contacted the army’s bomb-disposal team to arrange for the objects to be recovered.

Zaminur Rahman Khan, additional superintendent of police (Crime and Operations) in the district, told Prothom Alo that after the mine-like objects were discovered, the army bomb-disposal team was contacted. The site was also placed under police protection.

The army has recovered the mines and taken them into its custody. The process of neutralising them is under way, he added.

item.title: Bezos consortium nears deal to buy Liverpool stake: report
item.description:
SOCCER-FRIENDLY-LIV-ASM/

Amazon founder Jeff Bezos is part of a consortium nearing a deal to buy a one-third stake in Premier League club Liverpool, a report said Monday.

Sky News said Bezos was part of an investor group led by Amit Bhatia, the son-in-law of India steel billionaire Lakshmi Mittal, that also also includes Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin.

Liverpool owners Fenway Sports Group (FSG) confirmed the approach from Bhatia's group last month.

"An investment consortium led, managed, and represented by Amit Bhatia has expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club," an FSG spokesman told AFP.

Bhatia was until recently a shareholder in Championship club Queens Park Rangers.

The Sky report said the consortium was "closing in on a deal to buy a roughly one-third stake in Liverpool", with FSG preparing to make an announcement "as soon as this week".

Bezos, 62, is one of the world''s richest men, with a fortune estimated by Forbes magazine at more than US$280 billion, while Saverin's wealth is put at US$33 billion.

Bezos has reportedly explored previous bids for the NFL's Seattle Seahawks and Washington Commanders, but decided against pursuing either deal.

Sky said the investment in Liverpool, part of an influx of American money into the Premier League, would reportedly value the 20-time English league champions at US$6 billion.

FSG, which also owns the Boston Red Sox baseball team, bought Liverpool in 2010 for £300 million (US$405 million).

It sold a minority stake in the club in 2023 to US private equity group Dynasty Equity.

Liverpool won the Premier League title in 2024/25 under Arne Slot but the Dutchman was sacked in May after a turbulent season.

item.title: Dinesh Trivedi leaves for India after 3 important meetings in Dhaka
item.description:
Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh Dinesh Trivedi left Dhaka for New Delhi on Monday after holding three meetings in Dhaka over the past 24 hours, which is seen as further consultations amid efforts to engage constructively to take forward relations between the two neighbours.

He met Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman on Sunday at State Guest House Padma, while he had separate courtesy meetings with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed at the Secretariat on Monday.

“Yes, he left Dhaka for New Delhi (on Monday),” a diplomatic source told news agency UNB, without elaborating, adding that the visit was “preplanned.”

During the courtesy meeting with the Bangladesh prime minister, Dinesh Trivedi conveyed greetings from Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi to Tarique Rahman and the intent to work together with the government and the people of Bangladesh in a “positive, constructive and forward-looking” manner.

They exchanged views on matters of mutual interest and discussed avenues for further strengthening bilateral relations between India and Bangladesh with a people-centric approach.

During his meeting with Home Minister Salahuddin, they discussed areas of common interest, including security cooperation between the two countries, and ways to further strengthen bilateral relations.

The high commissioner conveyed India’s willingness to strengthen people-centric cooperation in all domains, based on mutual interest, mutual benefit and mutual sensitivities.

item.title: PM calls for building Bangladesh envisioned by July martyrs
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Monday urged the country’s people to work from their respective positions to realize the dream of a Bangladesh where people’s basic needs and rights are ensured, as envisioned by the martyrs of the July mass uprising.
“Those who were martyred during the July mass uprising wanted to bring a change to the country – a change through which people’s basic needs and rights will be established and they could at least live in peace,” he said.
The prime minister was speaking at a ceremony at the Cabinet meeting room of the Secretariat in the afternoon, where members of the families of Bangladesh Scouts members killed during the July mass uprising were honored and provided with financial assistance.
He said no one has the ability to repay the debt owed to the martyrs for their sacrifice, said a press release issued by the Prime Minister’s Press Wing.
“Those who were martyred gave their lives while fighting for a noble cause. To ensure due respect for their sacrifice, it is not enough merely to remember them. Each of us who are still alive must work for the country from our respective positions,” Tarique Rahman said.
Addressing Bangladesh Scouts, he urged its members to work for the country and its people and develop a spirit of standing beside people and protecting nature.
The prime minister also called upon them to inspire others to work for the welfare of the people.
At the program, 10 families of Bangladesh Scouts members killed during the July mass uprising were given special honors.
Tarique Rahman also handed over cheques for financial assistance and medals of honour to the families of the martyrs.
Bangladesh Scouts President and Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Ghani called for the contributions and sacrifices of those killed during the July mass uprising to be incorporated into the national curriculum so that their role could be passed on to future generations.
Education Minister Dr ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon, State Minister for Primary and Mass Education Bobby Hajjaj, Prime Minister’s Adviser Dr Mahdi Amin, and family members of the July uprising martyrs were present at the event.

item.title: 17 in one room, only one survived Saudi factory fire
item.description:
Hasibul, a resident of Dubai village in Atrai upazila of Naogaon, was the eldest son of his family. After completing his bachelor’s degree, he worked for a local NGO. He later lost his job and remained unemployed for some time before moving to Saudi Arabia three years ago in search of better opportunities and to support his family financially.
He worked at a sofa manufacturing factory in Saudi Arabia, where the workers also lived on the factory premises.
On the day of the incident, Hasibul was sleeping in the workers’ accommodation inside the factory while taking a daytime rest. Suddenly, a fire broke out at the factory, claiming his life.
Eight other workers were burned to death in the blaze, while another eight died from suffocation after inhaling smoke. All 17 victims were workers at the same factory.
Of the 17 workers, 16 were inside the accommodation when the fire broke out and died. Only one worker survived as he was outside the room at the time. The information was confirmed by the Bangladesh Embassy in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.
According to officials at the Bangladesh Embassy, the fire broke out at around 2pm at a Bangladeshi-run sofa factory in the Musa Sanaya industrial area under the Shifa police station in Riyadh.
The fire is believed to have originated from an electrical short circuit. Firefighters rushed to the scene and brought the blaze under control before recovering the victims’ bodies from inside the factory.
Eight of the victims were burned beyond recognition, while the other eight reportedly died from suffocation after inhaling smoke. Embassy officials suspect the workers were unable to escape because the factory gate was locked.
Workers at other factories in the same industrial area said 17 people were employed at the factory, with 16 of them killed in the fire. The workers also lived inside the factory premises.
As the factory operated at night, the workers were reportedly resting inside the facility when the fire broke out in the afternoon.
Habibur Rahman the only survivor
Habibur Rahman, a Bangladeshi worker employed at the same factory, was the only person to survive the devastating fire.
Habibur told embassy officials that he left the factory at around 1:30pm on Sunday to get a haircut. When he returned, he found the factory engulfed in flames. He said 17 Bangladeshi workers were employed at the factory. Sixteen of them were killed in the fire, while he survived because he happened to be outside when the blaze broke out.
DNA tests may be needed to identify bodies
Sixteen workers at the factory were killed in the fire, eight of them after being directly engulfed by the flames. Authorities are struggling to identify the victims’ bodies.
Mohammad Rezae Rabbi, Counsellor (Labour) at the Bangladesh Embassy, said the victims’ passports and iqamas were destroyed in the fire. Efforts are underway in coordination with the district administrations in Bangladesh and the Saudi authorities to establish their identities.
An investigating officer at the relevant police station in Saudi Arabia said fingerprints would be collected initially to identify the victims. If the fingerprints fail to establish their identities, DNA testing may be required.
Once the victims are identified, the Saudi authorities will issue death certificates. The bodies will then be repatriated to Bangladesh.
Thirteen of the 16 Bangladeshis killed in a devastating fire at a sofa-manufacturing factory in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, were from Naogaon, while two were from Natore and one from Rajshahi, according to the Ministry of Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment.
The fire broke out at the factory in the Musa Sanaiya industrial area under the Shifa police station in Riyadh.
The identified victims from Naogaon are Farid of Ujanpoi village in Atrai upazila; Shuvo and Suman of Dubai village; Md Rubel Pramanik, Md Kalim Uddin, Md Mohon and Md Suman of Gondogohali village; Minhaj; Hridoy of Boala village; Shahin of Naogaon village; Abdul Jalil and Majidul of Kharsrota village; and Sagar of Sadnagar village.
Thirteen of 16 Bangladeshis killed in Riyadh factory fire were from Naogaon
Rubel Pramanik’s father is Md Saidur Rahman, while Kalim Uddin’s father was the late Bazlur Pramanik. Mohon and Suman were both sons of Guffar Pramanik, and Majidul’s father is Majnu. The name of Minhaj’s village has not yet been confirmed.
The other victims were Shamim of Dighirpar village and Sabbir of Khajura village in Naldanga upazila of Natore, and Shyamal of Morugram-Dangapara village in Bagmara upazila of Rajshahi.

item.title: Miscreants attack Khulna newspaper office, assault staffer
item.description:
Miscreants attacked the office of the Khulna-based daily newspaper "Dainik Probaha" and assaulted a staff member early Monday. The attack occurred around 2:00 AM.
According to locals, the newspaper's Chief Pasterman, Faisal Ahmed, was working when he noticed a major commotion in the slum located behind the office building. When he attempted to observe the situation through a gap in the wall, several individuals entered the office and beat him before fleeing the scene.
Md. Rafiqul Islam, Officer-in-Charge (OC) of Sonadanga Police Station, said that police visited the scene on Monday morning following the report.
The OC mentioned that during initial inquiries, some residents claimed they entered the building out of fear that bricks were falling from the office structure into the slum.
The OC added that the police have spoken with the newspaper management and will take legal action once a formal complaint is filed.

item.title: Mother dies after 8-year-old son in Narayanganj gas explosion
item.description:
A woman who suffered severe burns in a gas explosion in Narayanganj died on Monday, two days after her eight-year-old son succumbed to his injuries.
Beauty Akter, 24, died while undergoing treatment at the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery in Dhaka on Monday morning.
Dr Shawon Bin Rahman, a physician at the institute, said around 80% of Beauty’s body was burned. Earlier on Saturday morning, her son Maruf died at the same hospital.
Beauty’s husband, Maidul, a mason by profession, is still undergoing treatment at the hospital with burns covering 85% of his body. His condition is critical, doctors said.
The explosion occurred around 7:30 am on Friday at a tin-shed rented house in Kuripara Chapatali area of Bandar upazila.
According to local residents, gas accumulated inside the house following a leak. Maidul reportedly tried to light a match to smoke a cigarette, triggering the accumulated gas and causing the explosion.
Three family members were severely burned in the blast. Locals rescued them and took them to the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery for treatment.
Abdullah Al Arefin, deputy assistant director of Narayanganj Fire Service and Civil Defence, said the explosion was caused by gas that leaked from a gas line in the kitchen and accumulated inside the house.

item.title: Tk1.21C robbed from Uttara fuel pump owned by to PM’s cousin
item.description:
Robbers have stolen Tk1.21 crore from a fuel pump in Uttara when employees carried the cash to a bank for deposit.
The fuel pump, DL Petrol Pump, is linked to Taseen Akhter Haque Del, maternal cousin of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman. Police have yet to arrest anyone over the robbery.
The incident occurred around 10:30am on Sunday, on a road south of the RAB-1 battalion. Several people riding three motorcycles intercepted the vehicle carrying the cash. They first rammed the vehicle, then attacked the employees with sharp weapons and snatched the money bag.
The attackers fled the scene with the cash.
The stolen Tk1.21 crore belonged to DL Petrol Pump. Pump manager Karim filed a case at Airport police station on Sunday against unidentified persons.
Airport police station OC Kamrul Hasan Talukder said police had not arrested anyone yet but continued efforts to identify and apprehend those involved.
“We have not been able to arrest anyone so far. However, efforts are continuing. We are analyzing CCTV footage from the area,” he said.
According to relevant sources, DL Petrol Pump handles around Tk45 lakh to Tk50 lakh in transactions every day.
The pump usually sends the day’s sales proceeds to a bank for deposit between 10am and 10:30am.
Banks remain closed on Fridays and Saturdays, so the pump deposits the proceeds from both days together on the following working day, Sunday. As a result, employees carried a comparatively larger amount of cash from the pump to the bank on Sunday.
The employees were carrying the accumulated cash to the bank when the attackers intercepted them.
Taseen Akhter Haque Del is associated with the ownership of the establishment.
He is the younger son of Khurshid Jahan Haque, sister of late former prime minister Khaleda Zia and a former member of parliament and minister.
Police are analyzing CCTV footage from the area to identify the attackers and establish how they carried out the robbery.

item.title: Ritu scores GPA-5 in SSC despite losing father during exams
item.description:
Ritu Khatun, a student of Hakimpur Secondary School in Chaugachha upazila, has secured a GPA-5 in the SSC examination despite losing her father during the exams.
A humanities student, Ritu sat for her exams while her father, Kabir Hossain, a day labourer and the family’s sole breadwinner, was battling cancer.
During the exams, Kabir’s condition deteriorated and he was admitted to Jessore General Hospital. On May 10, the day Ritu was scheduled to sit for her Bangladesh History and World Civilisation examination, her father died at the hospital early in the morning.
The family did not tell Ritu about her father’s death before the exam. She travelled from Hakimpur village, around 10km from Chaugachha town, to her examination centre at Sara Pilot Girls’ High School.
After Ritu reached the centre, her father’s body was brought home. She learned about his death only after returning home following the exam. After seeing her father for the last time and bidding him farewell, she had to return to her studies and prepare for the remaining exams.
Despite the devastating loss, Ritu completed all her examinations and secured a GPA-5 when the results were published on Monday.
“I am sure my father would have been very happy to see my result if he were alive. I ask everyone to pray for him,” Ritu said.
She said she was now worried about pursuing higher education as her family was struggling financially.
“Our family depended on my father’s income. Now that he is gone, it has become very difficult to make ends meet,” she said.
Ritu is the younger of two daughters of the late Kabir Hossain and Rehena Khatun of Hakimpur village under Hakimpur union. Her elder sister is married.
Shahana Khatun, a senior assistant teacher at Ritu’s school, said Ritu was a talented student and the school had expected her to perform well.
“Her father’s illness and the family’s financial hardship could not stop her from achieving this result. We hope she will continue to succeed in the future,” she said.
She also urged well-off members of society to support Ritu and help arrange a scholarship for her higher education.
Chaugachha Upazila Nirbahi Officer Farzana Islam described Ritu’s achievement as “very good news” and assured her of support from the upazila administration.
“We will stand by this determined and talented student and provide the highest possible support for her higher education,” she said.

item.title: Chhatra Dal, Shibir agree on peaceful coexistence at Alia Madrasa
item.description:
A week after clashes between Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal and Bangladesh Islami Chhatra Shibir activists, the two organizations have agreed to maintain peaceful coexistence at the residential hall of Sarkari Madrasa-e-Alia in Old Dhaka.
The understanding came at a meeting between leaders of the two groups, mediated by the madrasa administration. Following the meeting, Shibir activists returned to the hall around 2pm on Monday.
The dispute began on the morning of August 4, when activists of Chhatra Dal and Chhatra Shibir clashed at Jagannath University over participation in programs marking the second anniversary of the July mass uprising.
The confrontation later spread to the area in front of Alia Madrasa, where activists of the two organizations were involved in a prolonged clash.
After hours of fighting, Shibir activists withdrew from the area. Chhatra Dal activists later went to the hall, asked students to leave and locked the gates.
When Shibir activists tried to return to the hall on Sunday, they were stopped.
Later that night, the principal, vice principal and other administrative officials of Sarkari Madrasa-e-Alia met with leaders of both organizations to resolve the standoff.
BNP MP for Dhaka-7 Hamidur Rahman Hamid and Jamaat-e-Islami MP for Dhaka-5 Kamal Hossain also attended the meeting.
Chhatra Dal's Alia unit leaders represented the organization, while Chhatra Shibir was represented by its central publicity secretary and Ducsu GS S M Farhad, Dhaka Mahanagar Purba unit president Imdadul Haque Miazi and Alia Madrasa unit president Abdul Alim.
The two sides agreed to maintain a peaceful and mutually respectful environment in the hall and on campus. They also agreed to avoid activities that could trigger conflict, create disorder or disrupt the academic environment.
Speaking to Dhaka Tribune, Abdul Alim, president of Chhatra Shibir's Alia Madrasa unit, said Shibir activists faced no major obstacle in returning to the hall, although they had received occasional threats in the run-up.
Saad Chowdhury, a leader of Chhatra Dal's Alia Madrasa unit, also confirmed the development, saying Shibir activists moved back into the hall on Monday afternoon.
However, the two groups have yet to settle how many seats each will receive.
The broader issue of seat distribution will be discussed further, with Chhatra Dal and Chhatra Shibir expected to hold separate meetings with the administration.

item.title: Cooperation sought to build Bangladesh-Netherlands people’s partnership
item.description:
A Dutch delegation has sought cooperation from Khulna University (KU) to establish a ‘People’s Partnership’ between Bangladesh and the Netherlands.
The delegation, comprising Rob Vissers and Timo Koren of Hope XXL, Benjamin Loman of Vice Versa Global, and Jeanie Marissen of Utrecht University, paid a courtesy call on KU Vice-Chancellor Prof Dr Md Rezaul Karim.
During the meeting, the delegation members said the initiative could become a new-generation model of international cooperation, enabling young people from both countries to jointly develop social projects, schools and universities to exchange knowledge, journalists to share stories, businesses to collaborate on innovation, and local governments and public institutions to exchange experiences.
They expressed the hope that the partnership could eventually inspire similar initiatives between other countries and sought KU’s support for its implementation.
The vice-chancellor said KU has already collaborated with several Dutch universities, including Wageningen University & Research and Utrecht University, and assured the delegation of all possible cooperation.
He suggested setting up information corners during major university events, including KU Day on November 25, to highlight educational and research opportunities in the Netherlands.

item.title: Major quake rocks Colombia and neighbors, 18 confirmed dead
item.description:
A powerful earthquake rocked Colombia and neighboring Latin American countries on Monday, with at least 18 people confirmed dead in first reports as shocked residents surveyed destroyed buildings.
Emergency teams rushed to help victims and search for survivors in the rubble after geologists recorded the quake at a magnitude of 7.4 with an epicenter 100 km (60 miles) deep in the west of the country.
The early-morning quake was also felt in Ecuador, Panama and Venezuela -- itself hit by a devastating quake in late June -- and prompted building evacuations in the Colombian capital Bogota, AFP reporters saw.
News footage showed collapsed buildings across western Colombia, though officials said they did not fear a tsunami.
At least 18 people were killed in the city of Pereira alone, Mayor Mauricio Salazar told Caracol Radio, adding “the situation is critical.”
The governor of Colombia’s Choco province wrote on X that there was serious damage in the provincial capital Quibdo, where video showed collapsed buildings.
Choco was at the epicenter of the quake, and the death toll from the area was not immediately known.
Alejandro Eder, the mayor of Cali, Colombia’s third largest city, reported at least 20 buildings had collapsed and people were trapped as “major damage” that was being evaluated with drones.
News outlets aired images of buildings also destroyed in cities such as Manizales.
“There is no electricity or cell phone coverage. It was strong, really strong. Things fell in my house,” Martha Estrada, a 66-year-old resident of Eje Cafetero, which means coffee-growing region, told AFP.
“The quake was very, very strong,” said Valeria Polo, a 29 year old content creator in Bogota.
Six small airports in western Colombia suspended operations, the civil aeronautics agency said.
Bogota Mayor Carlos Galan said on Blu Radio that damage in the national capital appeared to be limited to cracks in the facades of houses and buildings.
President Abelardo de la Espriella announced he would travel to the quake-hit region.
In Bogota people ran out into the street in their pajamas as emergency sirens rang out, AFP reporters saw.
Twin earthquakes in Venezuela of magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 on June 24 killed more than 6,000 people and caused devastating property damage.

item.title: Major quake rocks Colombia and neighbors, 18 confirmed dead
item.description:
COLOMBIA-QUAKE/

A powerful earthquake rocked Colombia and neighboring Latin American countries on Monday, with at least 18 people confirmed dead in first reports as shocked residents surveyed destroyed buildings.

Emergency teams rushed to help victims and search for survivors in the rubble after geologists recorded the quake at a magnitude of 7.4 with an epicenter 100 km (60 miles) deep in the west of the country.

The early-morning quake was also felt in Ecuador, Panama and Venezuela -- itself hit by a devastating quake in late June -- and prompted building evacuations in the Colombian capital Bogota, AFP reporters saw.

News footage showed collapsed buildings across western Colombia, though officials said they did not fear a tsunami.

At least 18 people were killed in the city of Pereira alone, Mayor Mauricio Salazar told Caracol Radio, adding "the situation is critical."

The governor of Colombia's Choco province wrote on X that there was serious damage in the provincial capital Quibdo, where video showed collapsed buildings.

Choco was at the epicenter of the quake, and the death toll from the area was not immediately known.

Alejandro Eder, the mayor of Cali, Colombia's third largest city, reported at least 20 buildings had collapsed and people were trapped as "major damage" that was being evaluated with drones.

News outlets aired images of buildings also destroyed in cities such as Manizales.

''Strong, really strong''

"There is no electricity or cell phone coverage. It was strong, really strong. Things fell in my house," Martha Estrada, a 66 year old resident of Eje Cafetero, which means coffee-growing region, told AFP.

"The quake was very, very strong," said Valeria Polo, a 29 year old content creator in Bogota.

Six small airports in western Colombia suspended operations, the civil aeronautics agency said.

Bogota Mayor Carlos Galan said on Blu Radio that damage in the national capital appeared to be limited to cracks in the facades of houses and buildings.

President Abelardo de la Espriella announced he would travel to the quake-hit region.

In Bogota people ran out into the street in their pajamas as emergency sirens rang out, AFP reporters saw.

Twin earthquakes in Venezuela of magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 on June 24 killed more than 6,000 people and caused devastating property damage.

item.title: Fakhrul set for Bangabhaban, BNP braces for leadership, Cabinet shake-up
item.description:
BNP Secretary-General and LGRD Minister Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir is set to be nominated as the ruling party’s presidential candidate, a move that could trigger a significant reshuffle both within the BNP’s top leadership and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s Cabinet.
Multiple high-level BNP sources said the party has finalised Fakhrul’s nomination after its National Standing Committee entrusted Tarique with selecting the candidate.
According to the sources, Fakhrul has also signed the written consent required to contest the presidential election, although the BNP has yet to make an official announcement.
If nominated and elected, the veteran BNP leader would have to relinquish his posts as party secretary-general and LGRD minister, immediately opening two important positions in the ruling party and government.
Senior Joint Secretary-General and Prime Minister’s Political Adviser Ruhul Kabir Rizvi has emerged as the most discussed potential successor to Fakhrul in the BNP, while possible changes involving several Cabinet portfolios are also under consideration, party sources said.
The development comes just three days before the August 13 deadline for presidential nominations.
According to the election schedule, nomination papers can be submitted between 10am and 4pm on August 13.
Candidates may withdraw until August 18, while voting will take place in the National Parliament on August 20 if more than one candidate remains in the race.
The BNP has already collected two nomination papers from the Election Commission.
On Sunday, BNP Vice-Chairman and Chief Whip Nurul Islam Moni and Rizvi collected the papers from the office of the chief election commissioner.
However, Fakhrul publicly maintained that he had not been informed of any decision.
BNP Media Cell member Shairul Kabir Khan, quoting Fakhrul, said: “After being informed about the matter, the secretary-general said that he knows nothing about it. Nothing has been communicated to him by the party.”
According to BNP policymaking-level sources, the presidential nomination was discussed at the party’s National Standing Committee meeting on August 2.
The meeting ultimately authorised BNP Chairman Tarique Rahman to finalise the candidate.
Following subsequent discussions at the party’s highest level, sources said Fakhrul was selected.
Under the presidential election law, a candidate must provide written consent to contest and perform the duties of president if elected.
Party sources said Fakhrul signed that declaration on Saturday.
The BNP, however, is expected to formally announce its candidate closer to the nomination deadline.
Fakhrul’s possible move to Bangabhaban has already intensified discussion over who would take charge of the BNP’s day-to-day organisational leadership.
Multiple party sources said Rizvi is currently the leading contender to become acting secretary-general.
Rizvi did not contest the recent national election and was not inducted into the Cabinet, leaving him positioned to take on a larger organisational role, according to senior party leaders.
One possibility under discussion is appointing an acting secretary-general until the BNP holds its National Council, where a permanent successor could be selected.
Home Minister and BNP Standing Committee member Salahuddin Ahmed is also being discussed for the secretary-general post, although no decision has been finalised.
Fakhrul has been at the centre of the BNP’s organisational leadership for nearly 15 years.
He became senior joint secretary-general at the party’s fifth National Council in 2009 and acting secretary-general on March 20, 2011.
He was formally elected secretary-general on March 30, 2016.
During Khaleda Zia’s imprisonment and Tarique Rahman’s years in the United Kingdom, Fakhrul became one of the principal faces of the BNP’s political and organisational activities.
Fakhrul’s election as president would also leave the Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Ministry without its current minister.
Party sources said one scenario being discussed would see Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed take charge of the LGRD Ministry, while Water Resources Minister Mohammad Shahid Uddin Chowdhury Anee could move to the Home Ministry.
The discussions remain preliminary, however, and sources stressed that no Cabinet changes have been finalised.
Any reshuffle would come only after Fakhrul’s presidential nomination and election are confirmed.
Born on January 26, 1948, in Thakurgaon, Fakhrul began his professional career as a teacher before entering full-time politics.
He was elected chairman of Thakurgaon Municipality as an independent candidate in 1988 and later joined the BNP during the anti-Ershad movement.
He became president of Thakurgaon district BNP in 1992.
Fakhrul was elected MP from Thakurgaon-1 in 2001 and subsequently served as state minister for agriculture and later for civil aviation and tourism.
His elevation to the presidency would therefore mark not only another change at Bangabhaban following Mohammed Shahabuddin’s resignation, but also the end of a long chapter in which Fakhrul served as the BNP’s principal organisational face.

item.title: Educationists see system failure behind 19-year-low SSC result
item.description:
Bangladesh’s lowest SSC and equivalent examination pass rate in 19 years may be less a sudden “disaster” than the exposure of deeper weaknesses accumulated over years, educationists say, pointing to Covid-era learning losses, teacher shortages, curriculum changes, stricter assessment and prolonged instability in educational institutions.
Only 62.25% of candidates passed this year, down 6.20 percentage points from 68.45% in 2025.
Of 1,829,485 examinees, 690,608 -- or 37.75% -- failed, while GPA-5 achievers fell by 22,356 to 116,676.
Educationists, however, caution against interpreting the result simply as a collapse, arguing that it could provide a more realistic picture of longstanding learning deficiencies.
Educationist Rasheda K Chowdhury said: “It would not be right to call this a disaster. Because this may be the actual picture. We were unable to overcome the setback we suffered after Covid.”
She said corruption and mismanagement had also prevented investments in education from producing the expected results, while instability across the sector over the past two years had compounded the problem.
Rasheda identified shortages of qualified, subject-specific teachers as another critical weakness, particularly outside major cities.
She said: “How can a Bangla teacher teach mathematics? How can they teach English?”
The disparities become particularly stark when schools in Dhaka are compared with those in districts such as Kurigram and Panchagarh, she said, also pointing to inadequate instructors in technical institutions and weak monitoring of classroom teaching.
Education researcher KM Enamul Haque said this year’s candidates entered secondary school in 2020 carrying substantial learning deficits from primary education as schools remained closed for almost two years during Covid.
He said: “They came to secondary education with a major deficit from primary education and have progressed all these years inheriting that learning gap. This year’s results provide major evidence of that.”
Enamul also pointed to tighter assessment practices and disruption surrounding the 2024 student movement, saying prolonged instability may have affected students’ focus on education.
Md Rahmat Ullah, former principal of Kisholoy Girls’ School and College, similarly said stricter evaluation, curriculum changes, Covid-era learning losses and instability had converged.
Rahmat Ullah said: “Students have gone through a situation where they were not focused on studies due to prolonged instability.”
He added that curriculum changes had weakened students’ foundations, while online classes during the pandemic had failed to compensate adequately for lost classroom learning.
Education Minister Dr ANM Ehsanul Haque Milon, meanwhile, defended the assessment process, saying students received the marks their answer scripts deserved.
Milon said: “You can sing with an open heart, but you cannot give marks. The marks that were supposed to be given have been given.”
Taken together, the educationists’ assessments suggest the 62.25% pass rate is not the product of a single bad examination year.
Rather, it may be the cumulative result of learning losses Bangladesh never recovered, shortages it failed to address and instability that further weakened an already strained secondary education system.

item.title: Why are boys falling behind? Girls lead SSC results for 11th year
item.description:
Girls have outperformed boys in Secondary School Certificate (SSC) and equivalent examinations for the 11th consecutive year, widening a long-running gender gap that educationists say now warrants serious scrutiny over boys’ study habits, learning environment and growing exposure to distractions.
The divide was particularly pronounced in 2026.
While 66.68% of female candidates passed, the pass rate among boys was only 57.86% -- a gap of 8.82 percentage points.
Of the 911,000 girls who sat for the examinations, 607,939 passed.
Among 917,694 male candidates, 530,938 were successful, meaning 77,001 more girls passed despite fewer girls appearing for the exams.
Girls also maintained a clear lead in the highest grade.
A total of 63,896 female students secured GPA-5, compared with 52,780 boys, a difference of 11,116.
The pattern has now persisted for more than a decade.
Boys last recorded a higher SSC pass rate in 2015, when 87.41% of male candidates passed against 86.64% of girls.
Since 2016, girls have remained ahead every year.
The gender gap this year was visible across all three academic groups under the nine general education boards.
In science, 83.70% of girls passed against 77.39% of boys.
In business studies, the rates were 69.92% for girls and 59.98% for boys.
The widest divide emerged in humanities, where 54.38% of girls passed compared with just 41.14% of boys, a gap of 13.24 percentage points.
The latest results continue a pattern seen in previous years.
In 2025, girls posted a pass rate of 71.03%, compared with 65.88% among boys, while 73,616 girls secured GPA-5 against 65,416 boys.
Girls also led in pass rates and GPA-5 achievements in 2024, 2023, 2022, 2021 and 2020.
Educationists say the consistency of the trend suggests the issue goes beyond a single examination or cohort.
Acting Principal Mazeda Begum of Viqarunnisa Noon School and College said: “As a teacher, I can say that girls do more homework and prefer studying on their own. Boys, on the other hand, tend to be more restless.”
She said girls generally remain more closely connected to their families and receive greater supervision at home.
Mazeda said: “Girls can be described as more disciplined. Boys may have the same or even greater potential in terms of intelligence, but girls tend to be more disciplined when it comes to studying.”
Mohammad Shams Uddin, acting head teacher of Siddheswari Boys’ High School, also pointed to weaker study habits among boys, saying parents more frequently complain that their sons do not study at home.
He also cited mobile phone addiction and difficulties in maintaining discipline as contributing factors.
Dr Md Serajul Islam, professor at the Institute of Education and Research at Dhaka University, said boys’ greater exposure to activities outside the home could be dividing their attention.
He said: “Boys have many things in their minds beyond their studies. As a result, their concentration becomes divided.”
He cautioned, however, against interpreting examination scores as the sole measure of learning.
“Although boys are falling behind girls in examination results, boys may be learning more through experiences outside the classroom,” Serajul added.
He nevertheless warned that the persistent performance gap required greater attention from families, schools and policymakers.
Serajul said: “Our whole society needs to be quiet and calm. We have to create a better environment. If we fail to do so, there could be a major crisis in the future.”
Parents, meanwhile, raised concerns that gender is not the only divide shaping examination outcomes.
Nasrin Nahar, a parent of an SSC candidate, said students outside major cities often lack access to the same quality of schools, teachers and learning resources available in Dhaka.
She said: “Most of our students are from rural areas. If questions are not designed generally, rural students will continue to fall behind those in cities.”
At Viqarunnisa Noon School and College, GPA-5 achiever Rumaisa Ali Mershiha’s mother said: “Mershiha worked very hard. She was under a lot of tension because there were concerns about mistakes in some question papers. We were also worried about how the results would turn out this year, but the outcome is as we hoped.”
Another GPA-5 recipient, Mayarisa Hasan, said: “I missed A+ in one subject by just one mark.”
Experts say girls’ sustained dominance in public examinations represents a major educational achievement, but it also raises a growing policy question: why are boys increasingly falling behind at school?
At the same time, they note a striking contradiction beyond the classroom.
Despite outperforming boys in examinations year after year, many women later lose ground in employment because of family responsibilities, social barriers and wider socio-cultural constraints.

item.title: Same demand, different banners: DU women students split over hall curfew
item.description:
Dhaka University’s female students are pushing for the same basic reforms to restrictive women’s hall curfew rules, but three separate platforms have emerged, divided mainly over the extent of the changes and tactics to pressure the administration.
While many general female students have expressed solidarity with all three campaigns, their leadership largely reflects different political affiliations.
The “Boishommohin Nari Hall Chai” platform has a Chhatra Dal majority, along with two DUCSU leaders — Hema Chakma and Sanjida Ahmed Tonni — and two hall union leaders — Sanjana Chowdhury Ratri and Humaira Uponyas.
The “Nari Hall Songskar Andolon” has a Chhatra Shakti majority, along with DUCSU leaders, Chhatri Sangstha’s Sabikun Nahar Tamanna and Inqilab Manch’s Fatima Tasnim Zuma.
The “Oborodhbashini” platform has a left-leaning majority, with Biplobi Chhatra Moitree’s Israt Jahan Imu and Chhatra Union (faction) AGS Israt Jahan among its leaders.
At the centre of the dispute are three demands: extending or scrapping fixed entry hours at the university’s five women’s halls; allowing legally enrolled non-resident students to access their attached halls; and permitting female relatives of resident students to visit and stay overnight.
The fault line is over how far the curfew should be relaxed.
Boishommohin Nari Hall Chai and Oborodhbashini want the hall gates kept open around the clock.
Nari Hall Songskar Andolon is seeking extended entry hours instead, with students arriving after closing allowed to enter by showing their ID cards and registering their names at the gate.
Students say the existing restrictions have caused particular problems during medical emergencies and when they need care from family members.
A Rokeya Hall student once spent hours trying to get through the gate while seeking emergency treatment for an ear injury.
A Sufia Kamal Hall student said her mother was denied entry when she came to care for her daughter during a fever while she was sitting for final examinations.
“It’s an absurd rule,” she said. “My mother came all this way to take care of me, but no matter how much we pleaded, we couldn’t get her inside.”
The issue has surfaced repeatedly at the university, including protests at Mall Chattar in September 2025 and the Central Field in January 2026.
The latest campaign began on July 27, when Boishommohin Nari Hall Chai submitted a memorandum.
Oborodhbashini followed with graffiti protests at the gates of all five women’s halls on July 31 and later issued a 48-hour ultimatum to the administration.
Chamon Fariya Islam Meghla, a leader of the DU Chhatra Dal committee and a member of Boishommohin Nari Hall Chai, said the three platforms initially organised together before splitting over demands and tactics.
She said Chhatra Shakti and Chhatri Sangstha-affiliated activists did not want the gates kept open beyond midnight, while left-leaning groups wanted to lock the residences of administration officials as a pressure tactic.
Her platform rejected that approach and opted to pursue the demands through formal channels, she said.
Meghla also disputed the description of Boishommohin Nari Hall Chai as “Chhatra Dal-dominated”, saying only two to four of its leaders hold formal party posts, while the others are general students or DUCSU and hall union representatives.
Tanjina Islam, an Oborodhbashini leader affiliated with Chhatra Union, said the differences were substantive.
She said the Chhatri Sangstha-backed platform wanted only an extension of the existing deadline, while Oborodhbashini was demanding unrestricted 24-hour access.
She also alleged that the Chhatra Dal-led platform had engaged in undemocratic practices.
Tanjina said separate platforms could actually make it easier for politically unaffiliated students to participate, as many were reluctant to join a group dominated by politically affiliated activists.
Oborodhbashini’s memorandum carried nearly 1,300 signatures, collected exclusively from female students within a week, she said.
Nusrat Jahan Jerin, a Chhatra Shakti-affiliated leader of Nari Hall Songskar Andolon, said she initially launched the movement and invited all groups to join before they eventually split.
She said 24-hour access was the only fundamental point of disagreement.
Her platform wants the main gates kept open until midnight, followed by an ID-and-signature system for students returning later.
Jerin said the administration repeatedly cites security and coordination with other agencies as reasons for delaying a decision on round-the-clock access.
She described 24-hour access as “a luxury” for now, saying their canvassing found stronger support for extended hours.
The platform’s signature count has risen from around 500 to more than 2,000, she said.
As of early August, Oborodhbashini’s ultimatum had expired, while Nari Hall Songskar Andolon was awaiting a meeting with the vice-chancellor.
For now, the three platforms remain separate despite their overlapping demands, leaving the administration to deal with a movement united on the problem but divided over the solution.

item.title: PM greets disappeared BNP leader’s son on SSC success
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Monday sent greetings and gifts to Sadman Shihab, son of disappeared BNP leader Khaled Hasan Sohel, after he achieved an outstanding result in this year’s Secondary School Certificate (SSC) examination.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman congratulated Shihab on his achievement and sent him flowers, sweets and storybooks as a congratulatory gift.
After the SSC results were published on Monday, the prime minister instructed his Additional Press Secretary Atikur Rahman Rumon to deliver the gifts to Shihab.
Following the instruction, a delegation led by Krishibid Mokhsedul Momin Mithun, member secretary of ‘Amra BNP Paribar’, and coordinated by Atikur Rahman Rumon, visited Shihab’s residence in Banglabazar, Old Dhaka.
The delegation handed over the gifts to Shihab on behalf of the prime minister and wished him a bright and successful future.
Among others, ‘Amra BNP Paribar’ members Masud Rana Liton and Mustakim Billah, Chhatra Dal leader Abdullah Al Misbah, and Northern Students’ Forum Vice-President Farzana Rimi were present.
Khaled Hasan Sohel, former general secretary of the Sutrapur thana unit of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal, was allegedly picked up by plainclothes men identifying themselves as law enforcement personnel in Old Dhaka on November 28, 2013. His whereabouts have remained unknown for more than a decade.
