item.title: Home minister urges US businesses to boost investment in Bangladesh
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed on Tuesday urged US businesses to increase investment in Bangladesh, assuring them of a business-friendly environment and comprehensive security for foreign investors.
The minister made the call when a high-level delegation from the US-Bangladesh Business Council (USBBC), led by its President and US Chamber of Commerce Senior Vice President for South Asia Atul Keshap, met with him at the conference room of the Home Ministry at the Bangladesh Secretariat this afternoon.
During the meeting, they discussed various issues of bilateral interest, including ways to increase bilateral trade and investment between Bangladesh and the United States, as well as energy and security cooperation, according to a ministry press release.
The minister reiterated the government's strong commitment to creating an investment-friendly environment in Bangladesh and ensuring overall security for foreign investors.
He said Bangladesh currently offers ample opportunities for foreign direct investment (FDI), while the government has ensured a tariff-friendly environment for the convenience of investors.
Welcoming increased US investment in Bangladesh, the minister said the government has taken necessary legal and administrative measures to launch a one-stop service called "Invest Bangladesh" to bring the investment process under one umbrella and make operations easier.
He said administrative and legal facilities in this regard have been streamlined over the past five to six months.
The government is also examining various proposals for setting up LNG terminals at strategically important locations in the country, which would help diversify the energy sector and enhance overall national security, he said.
The minister further said major opportunities are being created for investment in food grain and energy supply, ranging from government-to-government (G2G) arrangements to private-sector investment.
He said initiatives have also been taken to introduce digital security measures, the "Safe City" project under smart policing, "Integrated Border Management" for border security and e-visa facilities to strengthen national security and technological protection.
Atul Keshap said major US companies have been successfully operating in Bangladesh for several decades and are currently among the country's major investors.
Highlighting Bangladesh's immense potential, he said the country's economy is expected to reach $1 trillion by 2034.
To achieve this target, he said, developing technical and managerial capacity, along with increasing GDP growth and tax productivity, is crucial.
He also discussed how US companies could provide comprehensive support and become partners of the Bangladesh government in the country's development process.
A 16-member delegation of business leaders from the US-Bangladesh Business Council, led by Atul Keshap, and senior officials of the Home Ministry attended the meeting.

item.title: JU English dept holds workshop on visual thinking, literary theory
item.description:
The Department of English at Jahangirnagar University (JU) held a workshop on visual thinking and idea generation on August 2, introducing MA students to creative approaches to understanding and applying contemporary literary and cultural theories.
Titled “Visual Thinking and Idea Generation,” the workshop was held from 11:30am to 1pm at the department as part of the MA course LECS 502: Contemporary Critical Theories and Pedagogies (Critical Humanities).
Cartoonist and illustrator Eeha Nawar attended the session as the guest speaker.
The four-credit core course introduces students to a range of theoretical frameworks, including Affect Theory, Ethical Criticism, Trauma and Testimonial Criticism, Medical Humanities, Posthumanism, Ecocriticism, Cognitive Literary Criticism and Digital Humanities.
During the workshop, Nawar demonstrated how visual arts, media texts and editorial cartoons can be used alongside literary theories to explore contemporary cultural and social issues.
She said literary theory was not confined to written texts and discussed how visual thinking could offer alternative ways of approaching complex theoretical concepts.
“Learn, study and understand the other side of the story. It helps develop critical thinking and contributes to building a strong character,” Nawar said.
Students participating in the workshop explored different methods of visualising ideas through art, including mind mapping, selecting visual elements and developing concepts across different media.
The session also covered the use of digital installations, graphic texts, cartoons and doodles as tools for developing and communicating ideas.
The workshop concluded with an interactive question-and-answer session, during which students discussed ways of applying visual media and digital humanities approaches to their course materials.
Other students from the department also attended the session.

item.title: Chief Whip: MPs bound by party line in presidential election
item.description:
Chief Whip of Parliament Nurul Islam Moni on Tuesday said members of parliament will not be able to vote in the presidential election, slated for August 20, against their party's decision as Article 70 of the Constitution remains unchanged.
“As Article 70 of the Constitution has not been amended, it will remain effective. No one will be able to vote beyond the party's decision. If anyone does so, their membership of Parliament will be cancelled,” he said at a press briefing at the Media Centre of Parliament after the 2026 presidential election preparatory meeting held at the Cabinet Room of Parliament.
Acting Speaker Barrister Kayser Kamal chaired the preparatory meeting. Opposition Chief Whip Nahid Islam and Whips Md G K Gouse, Rakibul Islam Bakul, Mia Nuruddin Ahmed Apu, Md Akhtaruzzaman Mia and A B M Ashraf Uddin Nizan also attended the meeting.
Speaking at the meeting, Acting Speaker Kayser Kamal said the state structure must be freed from fascism in all spheres.
“The 2026 presidential election is going to be held at a historic moment in building a fascism-free Bangladesh,” he said.
During the meeting, all necessary preparations, including the use of the Jatiya Sangsad chamber for holding the 2026 presidential election, all necessary logistical support and ensuring the attendance of Members of Parliament, were discussed.
The meeting also instructed completing all necessary preparations and providing logistical support for the election.
According to the election schedule announced by the Election Commission, the 2026 presidential election will be held in the Parliament chamber on Thursday, August 20.
The Chief Election Commissioner will conduct the election as the return officer in line with the Presidential Election Act, 1991. EC Senior Secretary Akhtar Ahmed, Parliament Secretary Golam Sorwar Bhuiyan and other senior officials concerned of the Parliament Secretariat were present at the meeting.
At the press conference, Chief Whip Nurul Islam said the BNP's candidate for the presidential election has not yet been finalised. “The party has entrusted the Prime Minister with the responsibility of finalising the candidate. He will announce the candidate,” he said.
He said the opposition has already nominated a candidate and the meeting was held to ensure a fair election.
“According to the election schedule, voting will be held in the Parliament chamber from 2pm to 5pm on August 20,” he said. Nurul Islam said the voting will take place inside Parliament and a ballot box will be placed there. Members of Parliament will cast their votes according to their division and seat number, he added.
He said preparations would be made to declare the result before the scheduled closing time if all 349 votes are cast within the first hour of voting. If it is found that one vote remains, it will wait until 5pm. After 5pm, the result will be announced, he said. The Chief Whip said the voting of the (Acting) President, Leader of the House, Leader of the Opposition and (Acting) Speaker would be broadcast live. After voting is completed, the counting of votes and the process leading to the declaration of the result may also be broadcast live, he said.
Opposition Chief Whip Nahid Islam said the presidential election should have been held in accordance with the “July Charter” to intensify acceptance and dignity of an elected president.
As the election was being held anyway, the opposition did not want to allow it to take place without a contest, he said.

item.title: BGMEA, LPP clarify FES Retail situation
item.description:
The Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) and Poland-based apparel brand LPP SA have issued a joint position regarding the ongoing dispute over invoices and outstanding payment claims surrounding FES Retail.
The joint statement was signed on behalf of BGMEA by its president Mahmud Hasan Khan, and on behalf of LPP SA by Dorota Jankowska-Tomków, director of purchasing and ESG.
BGMEA vice president (finance) Mizanur Rahman and LPP SA country manager Anna Staskiewicz signed as witnesses.
Both organizations stated that LPP is not legally responsible for the discussed outstanding funds.
Consequently, legal claims for collecting these dues should be directed only to the entities that are legally liable.
In a joint statement issued on Tuesday, BGMEA and LPP expressed their desire to work together to ensure legal certainty, worker protection, and a stable business environment and cooperation in Bangladesh's apparel sector.
The statement noted that the issue currently being publicly discussed primarily revolves around claims of outstanding liabilities involving contracts and invoices.
LPP is not a debtor regarding these liabilities and is not legally obligated to pay them. It has consistently cleared all payments owed to its direct suppliers and business partners in Bangladesh according to their respective contractual terms.
The joint statement mentioned that BGMEA has taken LPP's position into consideration.
The association believes that discussions regarding the settlement of relevant claims and liabilities should take place directly with the entities that bear the legal responsibility.
However, both parties acknowledged that the affected factories are currently facing difficult business circumstances.
In light of this, LPP indicated that it would cooperate in constructive dialogue if needed to resolve the issues by consulting with the legally responsible parties, though this will not alter LPP’s own legal position.
The joint statement also clarified LPP's recent review of certain sourcing activities in Bangladesh.
LPP stated that the main purpose was to ensure worker safety, legal certainty, and a stable, predictable, and fair environment for its business operations in Bangladesh.
LPP also clarified that this review was not an action directed against Bangladeshi manufacturers or factories.
At the same time, its commitment to fulfilling all legal and contractual obligations to its direct contractual partners in Bangladesh remains fully intact.
BGMEA and LPP stated that LPP currently works with more than 350 manufacturers in Bangladesh.
It is essential to ensure that disputes involving a limited number of third parties do not harm these manufacturers, the overall Bangladeshi garment sector, or long-standing business relationships.
For this reason, both parties emphasized refraining from generalized or misleading campaigns.
According to them, such campaigns could unintentionally have a negative impact on other garment manufacturers, workers, and Bangladesh's long-standing business relationship with LPP.
The joint statement added that this outreach will include protecting LPP officers and employees from any improper harassment, pressure, or unfounded legal complications.
However, BGMEA and LPP also reaffirmed their respect for the independence of the legal process and the right to raise valid claims against legally responsible entities.
This means if there are legitimate dues or claims, the concerned party will have the opportunity to raise and resolve them under the law.
Both parties pledged to work together to maintain a safe, stable, and uninterrupted business environment in Bangladesh while ensuring a transparent, fair, and mutually acceptable resolution to the ongoing dispute.

item.title: Banglalink receives BB approval to launch digital payment service Mukto Pay
item.description:
Banglalink, the country’s leading digital operator, today received a payment service provider (PSP) licence from Bangladesh Bank, paving the way for its entry into the country’s digital payments market.
Banglalink will launch its digital payment services under the brand Mukto Pay, a fully owned Banglalink service designed to provide customers with simple, secure and accessible digital payment solutions.
The milestone marks a significant step in Banglalink’s expansion into digital financial services, supporting the transformation of Bangladesh’s financial ecosystem, accelerating the country’s transition towards a cashless society, and contributing to its ambition to become a $1 trillion economy by 2034.
Designed to give consumers greater financial freedom and convenience, Mukto Pay aims to make every day digital transactions simple, secure and accessible.
Building on Banglalink’s legacy of helping make mobile connectivity more accessible to people across Bangladesh, Mukto Pay seeks to extend that impact to digital financial services by helping bridge the financial inclusion gap.
The service aims to enable individuals, micro-merchants and small businesses, particularly those unbanked or underserved by formal financial services, to participate more actively in the country’s growing digital economy.
Leveraging Banglalink’s nationwide connectivity, extensive customer reach and growing digital ecosystem, the service will particularly focus on broadening access to digital financial services for underserved communities.
The licence is part of the broader strategic vision of Banglalink and its parent company, VEON, to invest in and expand digital financial services in Bangladesh.
It also marks another step in Banglalink’s transformation from a telecommunications company into a digital operator, extending its presence beyond connectivity into digital and financial services designed to meet people’s everyday needs.
Johan Buse, chief executive officer of Banglalink, said: “Bangladesh’s journey towards building a cashless society and becoming a trillion-dollar economy will require greater financial inclusion and a digital ecosystem that enables more people to participate in the country’s growth. Mukto Pay is an important step in that direction. By combining Banglalink’s nationwide reach and deep understanding of local customers with VEON’s global digital expertise, we aim to make digital payments simpler, more accessible and more relevant to people’s everyday lives. This licence strengthens our ambition to invest further in digital financial services and contribute to building a more inclusive, cashless and digitally empowered Bangladesh, making a better life for all.”
Mukto Pay will facilitate a range of digital transactions, including money transfers, merchant and e-commerce payments, utility and government bill payments, salary and other disbursements, as well as other approved payment services.
Alongside its expansion into digital payments, Veon is also pursuing opportunities in digital banking and has applied for a digital bank licence.

item.title: MetLife Foundation, Midas to train 500 youth in mobile repairing and entrepreneurship
item.description:
MetLife Foundation, in partnership with Micro Industries Development Assistance and Services (Midas), has launched a two-year skills development initiative to train 500 youth in mobile repairing and entrepreneurship in Dhaka and Chattogram.
The program will equip participants with practical, market-relevant skills in mobile phone repairing and maintenance.
This will enable them to pursue self-employment and build sustainable livelihoods in a growing digital economy.
With over 187 million mobile subscribers in Bangladesh and nearly 75% of households owning smartphones, the mobile repairing sector offers strong income opportunities.
The initiative aims to bridge the skills gap and connect young people to these opportunities.
This initiative reflects MetLife Foundation’s commitment to improving economic empowerment and resilience in Bangladesh by supporting skills development aligned with market demand.
Speaking at the inauguration ceremony, Ala Ahmad, chief executive officer of MetLife Bangladesh, said: “Financial security begins with economic opportunity. This partnership with Midas represents a meaningful step toward empowering young people with practical and market-relevant skills. By investing in their potential, MetLife Foundation is helping to create pathways for sustainable income, entrepreneurship, and long-term resilience in Bangladesh.”
Parveen Mahmud, chairman of Midas, added: “We are proud to collaborate with MetLife Foundation on this impactful initiative. By combining our local expertise with global support, we can equip young people with the skills and confidence needed to succeed in today’s economy. This program will not only create employment opportunities but also contribute to building a more inclusive and resilient entrepreneurial ecosystem in Bangladesh.”
Established in 1982, Midas is a leading private sector development organization dedicated to promoting micro, small, and medium enterprises.
Through its technical, financial, and capacity-building services, Midas has played a key role in fostering entrepreneurship and job creation across Bangladesh.
MetLife Foundation continues to support financial resilience for individuals and families in Bangladesh.
Through initiatives like this, it reinforces its commitment to creating economic opportunities and supporting a more inclusive and resilient society.

item.title: Five arrested over attempted murder of BNP activist in Pallabi
item.description:
The Detective Branch (DB) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s Mirpur division has arrested five people, including the prime accused Rubel and Bappa alias Shakil, in connection with the attempted murder of BNP activist Alamgir Hossain in the capital’s Pallabi.
The other arrestees are: Hamidur alias Makhon, Parvez and Rabbi.
Mohammad Rakib Khan, deputy commissioner of the DB’s Mirpur division, said the five were arrested during raids in different areas of Savar, Gazipur and Kushtia on Monday.
Police recovered a pistol, two rounds of ammunition, two magazines, a private car allegedly used in the attack and a Volkswagen from their possession. They also recovered 1,000 yaba tablets, he said.
According to Rakib Khan, none of the suspects remained in Dhaka after the shooting. One was first arrested in Gazipur, while the others were later detained in Aminbazar, Savar and Kushtia.
The shooting took place at around 5:45pm last Friday when assailants got out of a private car and opened fire at Alamgir Hossain, 45, in Pallabi. A passerby, Jotsna, was also hit by a bullet.
Alamgir is undergoing treatment at Dhaka Medical College Hospital, while Jotsna was treated at Kurmitola General Hospital and has since returned home.
Alamgir’s wife filed a case with Pallabi Police Station over the attack, naming Mohammad Rubel as the prime accused.

item.title: LPP backtracks from its decision to suspend business with Bangladesh
item.description:
Poland's clothing brand LPP reversed its decision to suspend business with Bangladesh after it had recently announced the suspension due to payment complexities with Russian buyer FES Retail's pending dues to several exporters from Bangladesh.

Now, they will continue business operations as before.

In a joint statement, the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) and LPP SA announced the change.

The statement was signed by BGMEA President Mahmud Hasan Khan and LPP SA Director Dorota Jankowska-Tomków.

BGMEA officially informed the media of this today, Tuesday.

The joint statement mentions that BGMEA and LPP have agreed to ensure that business with over 350 Bangladeshi garment suppliers is not affected by the third-party dispute.

LPP is not legally obligated to pay FES Retail’s debts. However, maintaining its legal position, LPP will assist in constructive dialogue over the debt settlement.

BGMEA acknowledges LPP’s stance, stating that claims related to FES Retail’s dues should be directed to parties legally responsible for such issues. However, both LPP and BGMEA recognise that the affected factories are facing challenging commercial conditions. Any settlement discussions should occur with the parties legally liable.

The statement further emphasises that both BGMEA and LPP consider it crucial to avoid widespread or misleading information that could inadvertently harm other manufacturers, employees, or the long-standing business relationship between LPP and Bangladesh.

LPP has assured that the recent review of some of their sourcing operations in Bangladesh aimed to ensure the protection of their local employees, legal assurance, and maintaining a stable, predictable, and fair business environment.

This review was not directed against the manufacturers. It does not affect LPP's commitment to fulfilling all their direct contractual obligations.

There have been long-standing export dues of approximately $40 million owed by FES Retail to 40 Bangladeshi exporters. The exporters claim they had shipped garments to the company based on assurances from LPP's Dhaka office.

It has been reported that, last month, due to outstanding payments from Russian buyer FES Retail, owners of two buying houses filed separate cases against several officials from LPP’s Dhaka office in the High Court.

Following these cases, the police conducted night raids at the homes of multiple LPP officials.

On 21 July, LPP informed the BGMEA, the Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BKMEA), and the buying house owners’ association BGBA in writing that they had decided to gradually reduce their orders in Bangladesh.

On 31 July, LPP informed Bangladeshi suppliers via a letter that new orders would be halted and the development of new products with suppliers would be suspended.

Some suppliers of LPP have reported that the company purchased garments worth $700 million in the last fiscal year. LPP planned to import garments worth $770 million from Bangladesh in the current fiscal year. Based on this, they had begun placing orders.

item.title: 50th BCS viva begins, PSC sticks to announced roadmap
item.description:
The viva voce examinations for the 50th Bangladesh Civil Service (BCS) began today, Tuesday.

This marks the final stage of the Bangladesh Public Service Commission’s (PSC) plan to complete one BCS examination cycle within a year.

In line with the PSC’s roadmap, the viva has begun on schedule following the swift publication of the preliminary and written examination results.

According to the schedule announced by the PSC, the 50th BCS circular was published on 26 November 2025.

The preliminary examination was held on 30 January 2026. Just 11 days after the examination, the commission published the preliminary results on 10 February. A total of 12,385 candidates passed the preliminary examination.

The written examination was subsequently held from 9 April to 7 May. The results were published on 23 July, just 77 days, or two and a half months, after the examination ended. A total of 6,165 candidates were selected for the viva. Their oral examinations began today at the PSC office.

A total of 2,150 officers will be recruited through this BCS, including both cadre and non-cadre positions.

Of the 1,755 cadre posts, the highest number of appointments—650—will be made to the health cadre.

In addition, 200 officers will be recruited to the administration cadre and 117 to the police cadre, while a significant number of positions will also be filled in the education cadre. Candidates who pass the viva will receive final recommendations for these posts.

According to PSC sources, previous BCS recruitment processes often took a long time to complete. Job seekers had to wait for extended periods at every stage, from holding the examinations to publishing the results.

To address these delays, the PSC has set a target, beginning with the 50th BCS, of publishing the final results of a BCS examination within one year. According to the calendar, the PSC is scheduled to announce the final results of the 50th BCS by 25 November this year.

Delays in verification undermine benefits of faster results

Although the PSC has maintained its schedule for conducting examinations and publishing results, concerns remain over delays in final appointments.

The main bottleneck is the pre-employment background check, or police verification, which takes considerable time after the PSC makes its recommendations.

The Ministry of Public Administration oversees the verification and final appointment process. Because the verification takes so long, candidates are not receiving the full benefit of the PSC’s faster publication of results.

Despite the completion of various stages and recommendation processes by the PSC, the gazettes for the 45th, 46th and 49th BCS examinations have yet to be published.

Candidates fear that unless the verification process under the Ministry of Public Administration is expedited and the gazettes are published on time, their hope of receiving final appointments within a year will remain unfulfilled.

PM: State becomes stronger when people are economically empowered
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Tuesday said the state would become stronger only when its people are economically empowered, stressing the need to ensure economic capacity of citizens alongside political rights to build a strong and prosperous Bangladesh.
“Keeping ordinary people in hardship or silencing them cannot make a state strong. Political rights must go hand in hand with economic empowerment. To this end, the government will extend all necessary policy support to encourage domestic entrepreneurs to invest and create employment,” he said.
The prime minister made the remarks at a ceremony held on Tuesday at the Cabinet Division of Bangladesh Secretariat marking the signing of lease agreements to reopen three closed state-owned jute mills under private management, said PM’s Deputy Press Secretary Hasan Shiplu.
The government signed lease agreements with two private business groups to reopen three long-closed state-owned jute mills with around Tk619 crore in investment, creating at least 11,629 jobs and generating an estimated annual turnover of Tk1,175 crore. Under the agreements, PRAN-RFL Group will lease National Jute Mills Ltd in Sirajganj and Star Jute Mills Ltd in Khulna, while HAMCO Group will lease Platinum Jubilee Jute Mills Ltd in Khulna.
The prime minister said the government’s goal is to take the country to a stronger position economically and socially, and pledged necessary policy support to encourage local entrepreneurs to invest and create employment.
“If we can ensure the economic capacity of the people, the state becomes strong,” he said, emphasizing the importance of creating opportunities for people to improve their livelihoods.
Promising to stand by genuine entrepreneurs, he said: “If we can support entrepreneurs, it will create employment and livelihood security for people on the one hand and improve the overall economic situation on the other.”
The prime minister said the government wants to build a country where everyone would be better off than they are today. “We want to build a country where everyone will be better off than they are now. This is our main goal and objective,” he said.
Emphasizing the importance of domestic investment alongside foreign investment, Tarique Rahman said foreign investment would certainly come and the government wants it, but local investors and entrepreneurs must also be encouraged.
“We will provide as much policy support as necessary from the government to help them do business and make investments,” he said.
He said the government’s policies are aimed at creating opportunities for people from all walks of life, adding that the government is working with everyone’s cooperation to build a better and stronger country.
At the end of his speech, the prime minister thanked the two business groups for taking responsibility for the three jute mills and expressed hope that their new investments would succeed and contribute to the national economy by creating employment.
Commerce, Industries and Textiles and Jute Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir, State Minister for Textiles and Jute Md Shariful Alam, Textiles and Jute Secretary Sharaf Uddin Ahmed Chowdhury, PRAN-RFL Group Chairman Ahsan Khan Chowdhury and HAMCO Group Managing Director ATM Mustafa also spoke at the program.
The deputy press secretary said the three mills, which have remained closed for a long time, will be reopened under private management. Once operational, they are expected to generate at least 11,629 jobs, attract around Tk619 crore in investment and achieve a combined annual turnover of about Tk1,175 crore.
According to the agreements, around Tk157 crore will be invested in National Jute Mills at Raipur in Sirajganj. The reopened mill is expected to create 5,238 jobs and generate an annual turnover of around Tk500 crore.
Star Jute Mills in Dighlia, Khulna, will receive an investment of around Tk250 crore. Its reopening is expected to create 5,238 jobs, with a targeted annual turnover of around Tk500 crore.
Meanwhile, around Tk212 crore will be invested in Platinum Jubilee Jute Mills in Khalishpur, Khulna. The mill is expected to create at least 1,153 jobs and generate an annual turnover of around Tk175 crore.
The government has decided to reopen 20 of the 25 BJMC mills that remain closed under private management through leasing arrangements. So far, leases for 14 mills have been completed and possession handed over to the lessees, with production already resumed at nine of them.
Senior officials of BJMC and the lease-holding companies were also present on the occasion.

item.title: Voting in presidential election to be held on Aug 20
item.description:
Voting in the presidential election will be held at the Session Hall of the National Parliament Building on August 20, Election Commission (EC) Senior Secretary Akhtar Ahmed said on Tuesday.
“Voting will continue uninterrupted from 2pm to 5pm on August 20 . . . The extended voting period has been set to allow for any possible delay in the arrival of a member of parliament,” he told journalists after a preparatory meeting with the Parliament Speaker on the "Presidential Election" at the EC office in Agargaon here.
The EC secretary said the MPs would remain seated at their respective seats in the Session Hall, while election officials appointed by the EC would deliver ballot papers to them.
“Each ballot paper will have two parts - a stump and the main ballot. The counterfoil will contain the candidate’s serial number, the voter’s name, division number and a space for signature,” he said.
The names of the contesting candidates will be printed on the right side of the main ballot. The voting MP will write the full name of the candidate of his or her choice in the designated space beside the candidate’s name and sign the ballot.
Three transparent ballot boxes will be placed inside the Session Hall for the convenience of the MPs, and they will be able to cast their votes in any one of the boxes, Akhtar said.
He said vote counting would begin immediately after the voting ends at 5pm in the presence of the ballot boxes inside the Session Hall.
A ballot counting team, initially comprising four or five members, will sort and count the ballot papers.
Of the total 349 ballots, the chief election commissioner (CEC), acting as the election officer, will announce the number of valid and invalid ballots and the votes secured by each candidate.
The final result will subsequently be officially announced by the EC Secretariat through a gazette notification.
Akhtar Ahmed said arrangements would be made for live telecasting of the voting process from the Session Hall, while a designated area would be provided for journalists as well.
The EC will issue special identity cards to 20 officials involved in the election process, he added.

item.title: Three shuttered jute mills leased to private firms, 11,600 jobs expected
item.description:
Three long-shuttered state-owned jute mills are set to return to operation under private management, with the government expecting the revival to generate more than 11,600 jobs and mobilise substantial new investment as part of a broader drive to put idle public industrial assets back into production.
Bangladesh Jute Mills Corporation (BJMC) on Tuesday signed lease agreements with PRAN-RFL Group and Hamco Group for the three mills in the presence of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, according to the Prime Minister’s Office.
Under the agreements, PRAN-RFL Group will operate Jatiya Jute Mills Limited in Sirajganj and Star Jute Mills Limited in Khulna, while Hamco Group will take over Platinum Jubilee Jute Mills Limited, Khulna.
The PMO said the three mills, which have remained closed for years, will now be reopened under private management.
The government said the projects are expected to create at least 11,629 jobs, while the PMO release put combined investment at around Tk619 crore and potential annual turnover at approximately Tk1,175 crore.
The move forms part of a wider government strategy to revive shuttered mills owned by BJMC through private-sector leases rather than keeping the industrial assets idle.
Of BJMC’s 25 mills, the government has decided to reopen 20 under private management.
Lease processes for 14 have already been completed and possession handed over to the lessees, with nine returning to production.
PRAN-RFL Group has taken the two mills in Khulna and Sirajganj on 30-year leases.
The lease covers 37.97 acres belonging to Jatiya Jute Mills in Sirajganj and 45.99 acres of Star Jute Mills in Khulna.
At Jatiya Jute Mills, PRAN-RFL plans to invest around Tk500 crore to develop facilities for knitwear, woven garments, denim products, jackets, washing plants, handicrafts, bags, footwear and toys, alongside storage facilities for raw materials, packaging and finished products.
The Sirajganj project alone is expected to directly employ around 6,500 people and generate annual turnover of approximately Tk600 crore.
At Star Jute Mills, the group plans to invest another Tk250 crore to establish an environment-friendly industrial facility producing value-added jute products, furniture and medium-density fibre boards, among other products.
The Khulna project is expected to employ around 5,000 people and generate approximately Tk500 crore in annual turnover.
The investment and employment figures provided separately for PRAN-RFL’s two projects, Tk750 crore and 11,500 jobs, do not align with the PMO’s combined figures of Tk619 crore investment and 11,629 jobs for all three mills.
The discrepancy was not explained in the information provided.
Commerce, Industries and Textiles and Jute Minister Khandaker Abdul Muktadir, State Minister for Textiles and Jute Shariful Alam, Textiles and Jute Secretary Sharaf Uddin Ahmed Chowdhury and senior officials of BJMC and the lessee companies attended the signing ceremony.

The licence was issued under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2024, subject to the conditions set out in the central bank's letter dated Tuesday, August 11, 2026, according to a Bangladesh Bank notification.

item.title: Health minister urges coordinated action across ministries to achieve SDGs
item.description:
Health Minister Sardar Sakhawat Hossain has stressed the need for coordinated planning and joint initiatives involving all relevant ministries, saying the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) cannot be achieved by relying solely on the Health Ministry.
He said ensuring healthcare required more than medicines and syringes, with greater emphasis needed on disease prevention.
The minister made the remarks at a national conference on SDG implementation and review at the Bangadesh-China Friendship Conference Centre in Sher-e-Bangla Nagar, Dhaka, on Tuesday.
“Alongside education, law and order, and reducing gender inequality, we need to bring sectors such as water and social welfare together with the health sector to achieve SDG 3,” he said.
“SDG goals cannot be achieved with medicines or saline alone. Prevention must be the foundation, which the prime minister is giving the highest priority.”
Highlighting sanitation and hygiene practices in rural areas, Sakhawat said ensuring access to safe drinking water and raising public awareness about disease prevention were essential.
“We need to change unhealthy habits and lifestyles. People often touch dirty surfaces in markets and elsewhere and then handle money or engage in transactions without maintaining proper hygiene,” he said.
Referring to the water crisis in coastal areas, the health minister said people in the southwestern region were being forced to drink discoloured water due to shortages of safe drinking water and increasing salinity.
“I raised the issue at a conference in Paris last month, where we received assurances of international cooperation,” he said.
He also urged parents to remain aware of the harmful effects of excessive mobile phone and screen use among children, as well as the health risks associated with junk and fast food.
Calling on the Planning Commission to take a coordinated approach, Sakhawat said the SDGs could not be achieved by placing responsibility solely on the Health Ministry.
“An integrated plan involving the relevant ministries, including water resources, home affairs, social welfare and local government, must be developed,” he said.
“If the relevant ministries meet at least once every two months and jointly implement the plan, only then can we achieve the desired results.”
The minister also highlighted the need to prevent child marriage, raise awareness among mothers and promote breastfeeding. He also referred to efforts to promote vegetables and nutrition during the tenure of former president Ziaur Rahman.
“SDG targets cannot be achieved through isolated initiatives. They require joint action and coordinated implementation by all ministries,” he said.
The event was chaired by Professor Mustafizur Rahman, distinguished fellow of the Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD).
Water Resources Minister Md Shahid Uddin Chowdhury Anee, MP, attended as a special guest, while reserved women’s seat lawmaker Anna Minj was the guest of honour.
Health Secretary Md Kamruzzaman Chowdhury and Directorate General of Health Services Additional Director General Professor Dr Foara Tasnim, among others, were also present.

item.title: Doctors, students protest at DMCH, confine director over staff transfer
item.description:
A section of doctors and students staged a protest at the director’s office of Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) on Tuesday over the transfer of a hospital employee, confining Director Brig Gen Asaduzzaman to his office for nearly two hours.
Around 100 doctors and students gathered at the office and demanded the director’s resignation. The protest continued from noon to 2pm.
Fourth-class employees also tried to enter the director’s office but were stopped by the protesting doctors and students. They later took position outside the office.
Following the incident, the director general of the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) and leaders of the Doctors’ Association of Bangladesh (DAB) rushed to the hospital. Their intervention led the protesters to leave the director’s office.
DAB Secretary General Dr Md Zahirul Islam Shakil said the dispute was being resolved.
“The issue that caused the dispute is on the way to being resolved. Everyone has returned to their respective duties. The secretary and the DG of the DGHS are currently discussing the matter inside,” he said.
The protesting doctors and students alleged that the director was appointed during the Awami League government and was involved in corruption. They claimed a decision had been taken to transfer a hospital official accused of corruption, but the director blocked the transfer because of their alleged involvement in corrupt practices.
They also accused the director of being an ally of the previous regime and alleged that he had obstructed the treatment of students injured during the July uprising.
After the meeting, Health Secretary Kamruzzaman Chowdhury told reporters that the incident stemmed from a misunderstanding and had been resolved through discussions.
He said the dispute centred on the transfer of a hospital employee, whose transfer was later cancelled, allowing him to remain in his post. The entire matter would be investigated, he added.
The incident followed a dispute on Monday afternoon over the transfer of an administrative official. Doctors allegedly attempted to lock the official inside his office, but a hospital employee intervened. The employee was allegedly assaulted by doctors, prompting hospital employees and their leaders to gather in protest. The incident triggered a commotion on the hospital premises.

item.title: HC hearing begins on death reference, appeal in Magura rape victim
item.description:
The High Court on Tuesday started the hearing on the death reference and appeal in the case filed over the rape and murder of eight-year-old Magura rape victim.
The HC bench of Justice Bhishmadev Chakrabortty and Justice KM Rasheduzzaman Raja started the hearing in the morning.
Deputy Attorney General Md Imam Hossen Tarek represented the state.
A Magura court on May 17, 2025, sentenced Hitu Sheikh, the prime accused in the case and father-in-law of the victim's elder sister, to death, while acquitting his wife Jabeda Begum, and two sons – Sajib Sheikh, and Ratul Sheikh.
The rape took place on the night of March 5 last year, when the victim was visiting her sister’s house at Nijnanduali village in Sadar upazila.
She went to bed with her sister that night, but around midnight, her sister found her missing and began searching for her.
After a frantic search, the victim was found unconscious a few yards from the house.
She was initially admitted to Magura General Hospital and later transferred to Faridpur Medical College Hospital as her condition worsened.
The girl was then moved to Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) and later to the Combined Military Hospital (CMH), Dhaka, where she died on March 13.
The brutal incident sparked protests across the country. University students, including those from Dhaka University, staged demonstrations on their campuses demanding capital punishment for the accused.
Police arrested Hitu Sheikh and three of his family members in connection with the incident.
On June 10 this year, Chief Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury formed a special High Court bench to dispose of the death reference and appeal in the case on a priority basis.

item.title: Zahed: Hasina to get full security, legal rights if she returns
item.description:
Former prime minister Sheikh Hasina will be provided full security if she returns to Bangladesh and guaranteed all necessary legal rights if she faces judicial proceedings, Prime Minister’s Information and Broadcasting Adviser Dr Zahed Ur Rahman said on Tuesday.
He also said everyone would accept the court’s verdict in her case.
The adviser made the remarks while responding to questions from journalists at the weekly briefing at the Department of Information and Public Relations conference room.
“Hasina has said she will return in December. I have said many times that if she comes, she will come with full security. She will face the judicial process with fullsecurity and enjoy all her rights. Whatever is required under the judicial process will be ensured. Then, whatever decision the court makes, we will all accept it,” Zahed said.
Regarding Hasina’s extradition from India, Zahed said Bangladesh expected New Delhi to hand her over under the existing extradition treaty between the two countries.
“She was supposed to be extradited and brought back to Bangladesh. Bangladesh and India have an extradition treaty. We want the return of a convict sentenced to death. We want to bring her back to the country and bring her under the law,” he said.
The adviser accused India of not cooperating with Bangladesh over Hasina’s extradition and allowing her to engage in political activities while staying there.
“Sheikh Hasina is holding various meetings in India and recently even held a press conference there. India must sincerely consider these issues in the context of its future relations with Bangladesh,” he said.
“We want to bring her back and put her on trial, but instead she is sitting there and carrying out these activities. India must sincerely consider what the future relationship with Bangladesh will look like and how it will develop,” Zahed added.
He said Bangladesh had clearly conveyed its position to India regarding Hasina’s stay in the country and her political activities from there.
On Hasina’s trial, the adviser said ensuring the rule of law and protecting citizens’ rights remained the government’s position.
“We do not want to see a mafia regime like Hasina’s in this country again, and we will not allow such a regime in the future. This is not a fascist or mafia regime; this is a democratic state,” he said.

item.title: Home Minister seeks more Swedish assistance for Rohingyas
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed on Tuesday sought increased Swedish assistance to improve the living conditions of forcibly displaceds in Bangladesh.
"Their safe, dignified and sustainable repatriation to Myanmar is the only solution to the crisis," he said when Swedish Ambassador to Bangladesh Nicolas Linus Ragnar Weeks paid a courtesy call on him at his office at Bangladesh Secretariat, said a press release.
Describing the Rohingya crisis as a major threat to regional security, the home minister said Sweden’s role is important in keeping the issue in the focus of the international community as the country is the co-chair of the Rohingya Donor Group.
He urged Sweden to increase its assistance for improving the living conditions of the displaced Rohingyas.
The Swedish ambassador stressed the importance of safe repatriation and rehabilitation of the Rohingyas and reiterated Sweden’s interest in working for the education and overall security of Rohingya women and children.
During the meeting, the two sides discussed a wide range of issues of mutual interest, including security, prevention of irregular migration, expansion of trade, promotion of technical education and technical assistance, and a sustainable solution to the Rohingya crisis.
Referring to Sweden as an important development partner of Bangladesh, Ahmed said the government is placing special emphasis on modernising technical education to create skilled and globally competitive human resources.
He said plans and projects are being undertaken to establish new technical educational institutions at different locations across the country. The minister said demand for skilled manpower, including caregivers, is increasing in Sweden and other European markets.
He sought close cooperation from the Swedish government in improving the quality of technical education and training in Bangladesh and exporting skilled manpower.
The Swedish ambassador said Bangladesh is the only country in South Asia with which Sweden has a “Bilateral Cooperation Strategy.” He said Sweden’s trade relations with Bangladesh are deepening gradually, while Swedish investment is increasing in promising sectors, including readymade garments and healthcare.
The ambassador also said around 10,000 Bangladeshis are currently living in Sweden, a large number of whom are students. Expressing concern over irregular migration to Sweden, the envoy said some innocent people are becoming victims of irregular migration after falling into the traps of unscrupulous human trafficking networks.
In response, the home minister said the Ministry of Home Affairs is taking strict and effective measures to prevent human trafficking. He said aspirations for a better life and the lure of traffickers are the main reasons behind irregular migration.

item.title: Fishing resumes in Kaptai Lake after 3.5-month ban
item.description:
Fishing has resumed in Kaptai Lake after a three-and-a-half-month ban, bringing fishermen, traders and transport workers back to the lake and its busy landing centres.
The ban on fishing, fish transportation and marketing ended at midnight on Monday. From early Tuesday, motorised boats began arriving at the Kaptai fish landing centre with catches from different parts of the lake, including Bagaichhari, Langadu, Barkal and Bilaichhari.
The first boats reached the centre around 6:30am, carrying drums filled with kachki, chapila, tengra, ayir, baim, bacha, kaligunia and pabda.
The landing centre quickly became busy as fishermen unloaded their catches and traders prepared the fish for shipment. After paying the required duties, traders packed the fish in ice and loaded them onto trucks bound for Chattogram, Dhaka and northern districts.
A total of 28,866kg of fish were landed at the Kaptai centre between 6:30am and 1pm on Tuesday, said Jasim Uddin, head of the Kaptai Fisheries Development Sub-centre. The government collected Tk6.20 lakh in revenue from the day's catch.
At Rangamati Fisheries Ghat, traders said the first day's catch was dominated by smaller fish.
Md Shahjahan said adverse weather on Monday had prevented many fishermen from casting their nets, making it too early to assess the season's overall catch.
“Fish are generally smaller at the beginning of the season. Larger fish are usually caught later,” he said.
Commander Mohammad Foyez Al Karim, manager of the Kaptai Lake Fisheries Development and Marketing Centre, said a substantial quantity of fish had reached the landing centre by noon.
He said traders might be concerned about the relatively small size of chapila but expected the fish to grow larger within the next 10 to 15 days.
Foyez said the fish production target for the 2025-26 fiscal year was 8,500 tonnes, but actual production reached 10,000 tonnes, generating Tk22.60 crore in revenue.
The district administration initially imposed this year's fishing ban from April 25 to July 31 to allow fish to breed and replenish stocks. The ban was later extended by 10 days until midnight on August 10.
The reopening has brought relief to thousands of people whose livelihoods depend on the lake, while traders, transport workers and others are expecting increased economic activity.
Kaptai Lake, Bangladesh's largest artificial reservoir, is a major source of fish and hydropower and an important water transport and tourism route. Its resources are closely linked to the economy and livelihoods of people across Rangamati.

item.title: Dhaka-Gopalganj train service starts
item.description:
For Gopalganj residents who have waited years for a direct train to the capital, marked the end of a long journey — but the new service has arrived with a catch: its evening schedule.
The Abhijatri Commuter made its first trip from Dhaka to Gopalganj on Monday, opening a direct rail link between the district and the capital through the Padma Bridge rail route.
The train left Kamalapur Railway Station at 3:30pm and reached Gopalganj at 7:10pm. After a brief reception at Gopalganj Railway Station, it departed for Dhaka at 8:05pm.
The service will run six days a week, except Saturday, with 609 seats. The fare from Gopalganj to Dhaka has been set at Tk145, while the journey takes around three and a half hours.
Under the regular schedule, the train will leave Dhaka at 3:30pm and reach Gopalganj at 6:45pm. It will leave Gopalganj at 7:15pm and reach Dhaka around 10:30pm, stopping at nine stations.
The launch drew crowds to Gopalganj Railway Station, where residents gathered to witness a rail connection they had been waiting years for.
For many, the low-cost service is expected to ease travel to Dhaka for education, healthcare, business and employment. But passengers say the evening schedule limits its usefulness, particularly for students, traders and women.
Md Zakir Hossain of Khatia Garh Union in Gopalganj Sadar travelled to Dhaka with his wife on the inaugural train.
“We are extremely happy and excited that train service from Gopalganj to Dhaka has finally started after such a long wait,” he said.
But he urged the authorities to introduce a morning service.
“This is not just my demand; it is the long-standing expectation of the people of Gopalganj,” Hossain said.
Shabnur Khanom, a third-year honours student at Gopalganj Government College, said the train would significantly reduce travel costs for students.
“We often have to travel to Dhaka for job examinations and other purposes. A bus journey costs around Tk500, while the train fare is only Tk145,” she said.
She said a morning service would allow students to reach Dhaka earlier and reduce the risk of missing examinations because of traffic congestion.
For fish trader Motaleb Fakir, the timing is an even bigger concern.
“If the train left Gopalganj around 7am, we could take fish and other fresh produce to Dhaka and return the same day,” he said, adding that an evening service could force traders to stay overnight in Dhaka and incur additional costs.
Gopalganj Railway Station Master Ratna Baidya said the 609-seat service would operate six days a week and provide an affordable travel option for people heading to Dhaka.
The railway project connecting Gopalganj was taken up in 2010. The Rajbari-Gopalganj-Tungipara railway line was inaugurated in November 2018 after construction and renovation work costing around Tk2,110 crore.
Despite the railway infrastructure, Gopalganj had no direct passenger train to Dhaka.
That changed after the Dhaka-Bhanga railway line opened in December 2024 under the Padma Bridge Rail Link Project, creating the opportunity for a direct connection.
With Monday’s launch of the Abhijatri Commuter, Gopalganj has finally gained that long-awaited link — though passengers are already asking for a timetable that works better for them.

item.title: Jute cultivation exceeds target in Khulna region
item.description:
Jute cultivation in Khulna agricultural region has exceeded the seasonal target, with favourable weather, higher prices and growing demand for eco-friendly products encouraging farmers to expand the crop.
According to the Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE), farmers in Khulna, Bagerhat, Narail and Satkhira have cultivated jute on 38,361 hectares this year, surpassing the target of 38,287 hectares.
With the peak harvesting season now underway, farmers across the region are busy harvesting jute, while canals, beels, rivers and ponds have turned into busy sites for retting, fibre extraction and drying.
So far, farmers have harvested jute from 20,083 hectares, producing around 90,535 tonnes of fibre — about 51.9% of the region’s cultivated area.
During a recent visit to Terokhada upazila in Khulna, hundreds of men and women were seen working along the Atharobeki River and nearby beels in Baoisona and Kolabaria villages.
Women’s participation in post-harvest processing was particularly noticeable. Many women separate fibre from retted jute without entering the water, often taking jute sticks instead of cash as payment.
“I extract jute fibre in exchange for keeping the jute sticks,” said Jharna Begum of Kolabaria.
Tohura Banu, a first-year student at Terokhada College, said she helps her family process jute during college holidays.
“I enjoy the work, and it also helps my family,” she said.
Mahmud Gazi, who was working in the Atharobeki River, said a team of 15 labourers earns around Tk800 a day, while some workers are paid Tk5 per bundle.
Across the region, freshly extracted fibres can be seen drying on bamboo frames, bridge railings and around homesteads, while piles of jute sticks line village roads.
Farmers said favourable rainfall has made retting easier this year.
Mahtab Hossain of Baoisona village, who cultivated jute on three bighas, said heavy rainfall during Ashar and Sraban filled nearby water bodies, reducing the cost of transporting jute to retting sites.
However, frequent rain and limited sunshine have made drying the fibre difficult, he said.
Jute is also proving useful in maintaining the productivity of farmland between major crop seasons.
Soumen Bairagi of Golna village in Dumuria said farmers can grow jute between the wheat or pulse harvest and Aman rice cultivation, preventing land from remaining fallow.
“Early sowing in Chaitra also allows farmers to harvest jute in time for Aman transplantation,” he said.
Farmers also cited better prices and expanding domestic and international markets as key reasons behind the renewed interest in jute.
Trading of the new season’s jute has already begun at major markets in Khulna, including Khalishpur, Daulatpur and Khanjahan Ali.
Farmer Anser Ali said he sold freshly harvested jute for Tk3,700 per maund at Daulatpur market.
Veteran jute trader Fazlu Sharif, former vice-president of the Bangladesh Jute Association, said he expected prices to remain profitable for farmers and traders.
Jute is currently selling for Tk3,500-Tk4,500 per maund, with prices expected to rise further as marketing gains momentum.
Md Rafiqul Islam, additional director of the Khulna Agriculture Region, said average production currently stands at around 8.5 maunds per bigha and is expected to increase as harvesting continues.
“Abundant rainfall this season created favourable conditions for jute retting,” he said.
He attributed the rise in cultivation partly to increasing global demand for environmentally friendly products, saying higher prices have encouraged farmers to expand the crop.
The government has also provided incentives, while the agriculture department is supporting farmers through training and modern production technologies, he added.

item.title: Why did Israel reject Donald Trump’s 15-point plan for Gaza?
item.description:
US President Donald Trump triumphantly declared last month a “monumental step” on the pathway to peace in Gaza, with his Board of Peace reaching an agreement with Hamas to lay down its weapons.
Hours later he insisted Israel was “very happy” about the US-backed plan.
But it soon became clear the Netanyahu government had serious reservations.
Some of the deadliest Israeli attacks on Gaza in months followed the announcement, and then on Sunday, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu rejected the 15-point peace plan.
“They have ideas, some of them are acceptable to us and some are unacceptable to us,”
he said.
“Israel rejects the 15-point plan.”
He said at the cabinet meeting that Israeli forces would not withdraw from the enclave until Hamas was “genuinely disarmed.”
So, what’s actually happening here, and how does politics play into it ahead of an Israeli election?
Under Mr Trump’s proposed peace deal, Board of Peace officials said Hamas and other fighters groups would lay down their arms.
But Hamas said the concession came with conditions.
Specifically, the fighters’ group said its weapons would be stored and supervised by a new Palestinian technocratic committee backed by the United States and the Board of Peace to run Gaza.
The vetted international group is known as the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG). It has not been allowed to enter the strip by Israel, and is conducting its affairs from the Egyptian capital, Cairo.
A draft of the proposal reported in various media outlets described the terms of the agreement as:
“A process for inventorying and storing heavy weapons, military production sites, weapons depots, and tunnels shall commence. “This process is linked to a phased Israeli withdrawal from the areas it controls in Gaza and the inventorying of weapons held by armed militias in accordance with section 10 of this plan.”
Mkhaimar Abusada, associate professor of political science at Al-Azhar University in Gaza, currently based in Cairo, said it was a “big step” by Hamas to make the concession to disarm.
“They have basically, for the past 10 months, have refrained or have rejected the very essence of the idea of disarming themselves,” he told the ABC.
“Now coming publicly and agreeing to disarm and to turn all heavy weapons and light weapons to the Palestinian committee for the administration of Gaza in NCAG — that in my opinion is a very big development.”
The exact mechanism of how weapons would be handed over and stored was not clear.
Hamas also said it would only hand over the weapons if Israel stopped attacking the strip and withdrew its forces to the Yellow Line — the original boundary of territory inside Gaza controlled by the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) under the October 2025 ceasefire deal.
In recent months Israeli forces have continued encroaching deeper into Hamas-controlled territory in Gaza, increasing its share of land from more than 50% in October, to more than 60%.
Earlier this year, Mr Netanyahu had given orders to push even further to 70%.
Senior members of the Board of Peace, including its High Representative for Gaza, Nickolay Mladenov, visited Israel and immediately pressed the Netanyahu government to play its part in the progress towards peace.
The trip came after a series of statements from Mr Mladenov which appeared to be thinly veiled criticisms of Israel.
“What the agreement says matters. What happens next matters even more. Implementation and verification have to be real. Withdrawal must move in lock-step with decommissioning,” he said soon after Mr Trump’s announcement.
Then after Israel’s deadly strikes on the strip, Mr Mladenov wrote on X: “Two days of strikes across Gaza have killed civilians and destroyed medical supplies that people depend on.”
He added that it had followed “intense efforts” to get Hamas to agree.
After the Board of Peace meeting with the Israeli government, the Board of Peace issued a statement seemingly clarifying that sequencing problem.
“Contrary to inaccurate reports, we note that the withdrawal of the IDF beyond the Yellow Line will take place only once decommissioning is complete, as Hamas committed to the mediators,” it said.
“This applies to light weapons, heavy weapons, and the tunnels alike.”
Despite pressure from the Board of Peace, Mr Netanyahu has rejected the plan after Israel’s far-right government figures declared it “not acceptable” to Israel.
The Israeli military “will not carry out any withdrawal until Hamas is genuinely disarmed and will continue to thwart threats against our forces and our citizens”, the prime minister said.
The suggestion the deal would allow Hamas to keep its weapons inside the strip, regardless of who was controlling or supervising them, was not a welcome development.
“Leaving Hamas with the ability to rearm themselves within a couple of minutes is extremely dangerous because at the end of the day Hamas has not changed,” Yossi Kuperwasser, a brigadier general in the IDF reserves and the director of the Jerusalem Institute for Strategy and Security, told the ABC.
“There’s one point missing in these points of the new agreement. The first article of the [October 2025] 20-point plan was that Gaza is going to be de-radicalized. There’s no reference to de-radicalization here.
“So we are left with a radical Hamas governing Gaza and still very forceful, capable of rearming itself.
“If we withdraw from Gaza under these conditions Hamas is going to be on the footstep, on the doorstep of the same villages and communities that it attacked on October 7th.”
Hamas announced last month it had dissolved its emergency government in Gaza to allow NCAG to take over.
But Israel has described that as symbolic rather than anything of substance, accusing Hamas of keeping key officials in roles across Gaza’s bureaucracy.
There was also an issue of sequencing since Hamas’ statement suggested it would disarm once Israel had pulled back to the Yellow Line.
Israel, on the other hand, had long insisted it would only pull back once disarmament was completed.
Perhaps some of the debate there had come from Mr Trump’s post on Truth Social, which said “as disarmament is completed, Israeli forces will withdraw.”
Senior Israeli officials have also rejected the idea that the country had to stop its strikes on Gaza. They insist Hamas still poses a threat.
Since October 2025, when a truce was announced, Palestinian health authorities reported more than 1,200 people had been killed in Israeli strikes, among them many women and children.
Palestinians are in despair about whether Mr Trump’s declaration will change much on the ground.
Israel’s rejection of the US-backed Board of Peace road map for postwar Gaza has reportedly left Washington unfazed.
A senior US official told Axios the White House “is not bothered” by Mr Netanyahu’s statement on the Gaza plan and saw it as part of the election season in Israel.
“We understand Bibi’s political needs. We have no problem with it as long as he continues to do what we ask — especially regarding restraining attacks in Gaza,” the US official said.
Brigadier General Kuperwasser said assessments or estimates of Hamas’ weapons stockpiles were not public this far into the war, which is quickly approaching its third anniversary.
“We assume that the number of heavy weapons, the rockets, is relatively small, but we don’t know,” he said.
“[The deal] refers to only some parts of the equipment of Hamas, the heavy weapons and mainly the rockets, which they have not used for ages now.
“So how do we know if they actually gave all of the rockets or not?”
The issue of “personal weapons”, like guns, is slightly different. The draft of the proposal said:
“Personal weapons in Gaza shall be subject to the provisions of relevant Palestinian laws.
“The National Committee, as the transitional authority in Gaza, shall be the sole authority for registering weapons, issuing and revoking licenses, and enforcing the law, including through reintegration and social support.”
“I think the Israelis are saying something between 50,000 to 60,000 pieces of light weapons are still in Gaza, still in the hands of Hamas, other Palestinian factions, and also in the hands of families and clans in Gaza,” Dr Abusada said.
“I think it’s not going to be an easy task to go from door to door and collect all those light weapons.
“But let’s also face it that these [are] light weapons, I don’t think that they pose any threat to the Israeli side or any threat even to the communities next to the borders with Gaza.”
Dr Abusada rejected the idea that this was a “new deal,” as some in the Israeli establishment had quickly argued.
“It’s the implementation of phase two of President Donald Trump’s plan which was basically signed in October of 2025,” he said.
Both Brigadier General Kuperwasser and Dr Abusada said the upcoming Israeli election could have an effect on how quickly progress is made from this point.
It is currently scheduled to take place on October 27.
“I don’t think this is going to be a contested issue in the election,” Brigadier General Kuperwasser said.
“If Netanyahu is going to accept it he’s going to be heavily criticized by his opponents. If anybody accepts [they are] going to be criticized.
“I think that the only people who are going to accept it are the Arab Lists and maybe the Democrats — maybe. I’m not even sure about that.”
That likely means little movement prior to the end of October.
“We are not expecting that Netanyahu and coalition governments are going to … go smoothly with the implementation of this latest deal,” Dr Abusada said.
“But at the end of the day I think most expect that maybe the next Israeli government, or the government that will be formed after Israeli elections, will have to carry out these understandings or this deal.”

item.title: AIUB, Russian House in Dhaka to strengthen academic and cultural cooperation
item.description:
Alexandra A Khlevnoy, first secretary of the Embassy of the Russian Federation in the People’s Republic of Bangladesh and director of the Russian House in Dhaka, paid a formal visit to American International University-Bangladesh (AIUB) on August 9 to explore opportunities for strengthening academic, educational, cultural, and youth cooperation.
Khlevnoy was accompanied by Proshanta Kumar Barman and Delwar Hossain from the Russian House in Dhaka.
During the visit, a formal meeting was held with the senior leadership and representatives of AIUB.
The discussions focused on a range of potential areas of collaboration, including cultural and educational programs, scholarship and higher education opportunities in Russia, Russian language learning, youth initiatives, joint seminars and events, and opportunities for future institutional cooperation, including the possibility of establishing Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with universities in Russia.
Khlevnoy briefed the AIUB representatives on the activities and initiatives of the Russian House in Dhaka, highlighting its role in promoting Russian education, science, culture, language learning, and international youth cooperation in Bangladesh.
She also discussed potential opportunities for AIUB students and faculty members to participate in educational, cultural, and youth-focused programs supported by Russian institutions.
The AIUB representatives expressed their interest in expanding the University’s international academic and cultural engagement and exploring mutually beneficial initiatives with the Russian House in Dhaka and relevant institutions in the Russian Federation.
Both sides emphasized the importance of creating opportunities for students and faculty members through academic exchanges, scholarships, research collaboration, cultural programs, and joint educational activities.
The meeting was attended by the following representatives from AIUB: Prof Saiful Islam, vice chancellor; Shania Mahia Abedin, member, board of trustees; Prof Md Abdur Rahman, pro-vice chancellor; Group Captain (retd) Mohammad Zahidul Islam Khan, registrar; SAM Manzur H Khan; Abu Mia Akanda Tuhin; Md Manirul Islam; and Saadi Islam.
The visit concluded with both sides expressing their interest in maintaining dialogue and pursuing concrete initiatives to further strengthen educational, cultural, and youth cooperation among AIUB, the Russian House in Dhaka, and partner institutions in Russia.
